title: A scheduler simulator
description:
Simulate the round-robin scheduler of lesson 6.02 on one CPU core, and see how long everyone waits.

The first input line is the **time slice**. Each following line is a process: a name, its arrival time and how long it needs to run (its **burst**). Read until the end of the input.

```
3
A 0 5
B 1 3
C 2 1
```

The rules:
- Time starts at 0. A process joins the back of the **ready queue** at its arrival time. (Processes that arrive at the same time join in the order they were listed.)
- The CPU takes the process at the front of the queue and runs it for one time slice, or less if it finishes sooner.
- If it still needs time, it goes to the back of the queue, **after** any processes that arrived up to the moment its slice ended.
- When the queue is empty, the CPU is **idle** until the next arrival.

Print every stretch of time, joining back-to-back stretches of the same process (or of idle) into one: `t=START-END NAME`. Then, in the order the processes were listed, when each finished and how long it waited (finish − arrival − burst), and finally the average wait with two decimals. For the example:

```
t=0-3 A
t=3-6 B
t=6-7 C
t=7-9 A
A finished at 9, waited 4
B finished at 6, waited 2
C finished at 7, waited 4
Average wait: 3.33
```

There is always at least one process, and every burst is at least 1.
hints: After a slice, call `admit(clock)` **before** putting the unfinished process back on the queue: that is what puts newly arrived processes ahead of it.

`min(a, b)` is the smaller of two numbers: a process runs for `min(slice_length, time_left)`. `sorted(processes, key=lambda p: p["arrival"])` gives the processes in order of arrival (`sorted` keeps processes with equal arrival times in their listed order). `queue.pop(0)` takes the first item off a list and `queue.append(x)` adds one at the end: first in, first out.
requirements: Keep a ready queue (a list used first in, first out) and a clock.
Write a function that adds every process that has arrived by a given time to the queue.
